The core challenge lies in bridging the domain gap between synthetic and real-world data while ensuring robust generalization. The proposed method leverages volumetric feature sampling grounded in consensus and diversity principles, enabling effective fusion of multi-view information. This process involves projecting 2D heatmaps into 3D space using intersection/union masking, which acts as a dual constraint mechanism—ensuring both agreement and variation across views. The resulting volumetric features are then fused with adaptive weights that reflect per-view consistency, forming a kernel of multi-view reliability. Progressive regression from 2D representations ensures that each stage builds upon previous estimates, refining accuracy iteratively. These operations collectively form a structured pipeline where synthetic data mitigate lack of real-world annotations, yet remain constrained by the fidelity of rendering and camera modeling. The system's resilience hinges on the ability to maintain perceptual alignment between synthetic training and test-time deployment, particularly under novel viewpoints or lighting conditions.
